sections.overview: Amphilophus flaveolus is a cichlid endemic to Lake Apoyo, Nicaragua, and one of several related species confined to that crater lake.
sections.identification: It has a high, laterally compressed body and a benthic form distinct within the lake’s cichlid flock. FishBase reports 13.6 cm maximum standard length for a male or unsexed fish; the original 18-specimen series ranged from 9.22 to 13.64 cm standard length. Males and females have similar coloration: breeding adults become dark green-black with vertical bars, while nonbreeding fish are paler green-gray with flank spots. No reliable body height, width or mass figures were found.
sections.habitat: It inhabits freshwater in Lake Apoyo, a volcanic crater lake in Nicaragua. It nests on sand or mud in water less than 2 m deep.
sections.diet: Species-specific field data on prey and feeding are sparse; the reviewed taxonomic and conservation sources do not provide a measured wild diet for this fish.
sections.behavior: This fish defends a breeding site. In Lake Apoyo it is one of the territorial substrate-brooding cichlids.
sections.reproduction: This species is a substrate brooder with care from both parents. Lake Apoyo Midas cichlids breed mainly from November to January.
sections.ecology: It is part of an endemic species flock whose members differ in body shape and ecology despite sharing the same isolated lake.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment lists Amphilophus flaveolus as Critically Endangered (CR), assessed in 2019; its restriction to Lake Apoyo makes the lake’s condition central to conservation.
